crop.notes: Continuation of Wray's Column from page one; the 'In Bare Knuckle Days' section about Allen is complete across both pieces.

ocr.notes: Transcript skips the opening of the Allen section (Allen defeating McCoole on an island opposite St. Louis; first fight where the crowd broke in and the intimidated referee gave McCoole the win on a foul) and merges sentences, so it reads as if Allen regained the title from the crowd. Also omits the Boston racing section, 'Will Max Set a Record?' opening, Allen's height/weight paragraph and the closing paragraph. What is transcribed is accurate.

title.suggested: Wray's Column: Allen regained the title from McCoole in St. Louis

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch recalled that Tom Allen regained the championship by beating Mike McCoole on a Mississippi island opposite St. Louis, after losing their first fight on a foul when the crowd intimidated the referee.

metadata.notes: No page image; masthead not checked.

facts.fact: In their first fight Allen was beating Mike McCoole when the crowd broke into the ring and the intimidated referee declared McCoole the winner on a foul; McCoole then claimed the title
Allen easily defeated Mike McCoole in a return match advertised as a championship fight, held on an island in the Mississippi opposite St. Louis, regaining the championship
places: Island in the Mississippi opposite St. Louis

facts.fact: Before leaving England to settle in St. Louis, Allen fought a 35-round draw with Joe Goss
Allen lost all claim to the title when Joe Goss beat him on a foul after 29 rounds in Kentucky
Allen was only 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighed under 175 pounds

notes: 1935 retrospective by the Post-Dispatch columnist; dates are the columnist's recollection (no year given for the McCoole fights; '1873' inferred from context and other columns, so treat as approximate).
